issues.legal_issue: A written agreement specifying a sale, consideration, payment terms, and consequences for breach remains an agreement for sale rather than a loan merely because it includes quantified remedies for breach.
material_facts: The parties signed a document describing the owner’s agreement to sell the identified property for a fixed price, with an advance and further payments due before execution of a registered sale deed.
The document provided financial consequences for breach by either party, and the same amount of damages was specified for each party’s breach.
The document was attested by witnesses who testified at trial, and the agreement’s terms did not indicate that it was not intended to be acted upon.
The parties continued their landlord–tenant relationship until a sale deed was executed, a course the court found was consistent with the written agreement.
issues.conclusion: The document was an agreement for sale, not a loan transaction, and its breach clauses did not prevent specific performance.
issues.legal_principle: A document must be read as a whole, and the parties’ intention is gathered from the document itself. Quantified damages for breach do not, without more, show that an agreement for sale is a loan or that the sale was not intended to proceed. The court distinguished Dadarao v. Ramrao and relied on P.D’ Souza v. Shondrilo Naidu, which treated Dadarao as per incuriam for failing to consider Section 23 of the Specific Relief Act, 1963 and the binding decision in M.L. Devender Singh. Jai Narain Parasrampuria v. Pushpa Devi Saraf also supports the proposition that a damages stipulation does not establish that an agreement was not for sale.

rule.if: specific_performance_suit and signed_sale_document and fixed_sale_terms and mutual_breach_remedies

predicates.specific_performance_suit: A party brought a proceeding seeking specific performance of a purported agreement to sell property.
predicates.signed_sale_document: The parties signed a document expressing an agreement by one party to sell property to the other.
predicates.fixed_sale_terms: The document specified the sale price, payment arrangements, and conveyance after payment.
predicates.mutual_breach_remedies: The document specified financial consequences for breach by each party.

issues.definition: When a specific-performance suit concerns a signed document with fixed sale terms and remedies for breach by both parties, the document is treated as an agreement for sale rather than a loan.

issues.legal_issue: An increase in the value of property, by itself, is not a sufficient reason to refuse specific performance of a lawful agreement for sale.
material_facts: The courts below found that the parties had entered into a genuine agreement for sale and decreed specific performance.
The seller had received further payment after entering into the agreement and had also entered into other agreements concerning the same property.
The seller argued that the rise in property prices meant the court should not exercise its discretion to order specific performance.
The courts below rejected the seller’s reliance on an alleged earlier agreement with a relative, which the court found had not been acted upon.
issues.conclusion: The increase in the property’s price did not justify refusing specific performance, and the decree was upheld.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 20 of the Specific Relief Act, 1963, the court exercises discretion in deciding whether to grant specific performance, but an increase in the price of immovable property, by itself, is not a ground to refuse enforcement of a lawful agreement for sale. The court relied on P.D’ Souza v. Shondrilo Naidu and Jai Narain Parasrampuria v. Pushpa Devi Saraf.

predicates.specific_performance_appeal: A party appealed a decree granting specific performance of an agreement to sell property.
predicates.lawful_sale_agreement: The courts found that the parties had made a genuine and lawful agreement for sale.
predicates.seller_relies_on_price_increase: The seller relied on an increase in the property’s value as a reason to refuse specific performance.

issues.definition: In an appeal from a specific-performance decree, when a lawful sale agreement is established, a seller’s reliance on increased property value alone does not justify refusing specific performance.

issues.legal_issue: Concurrent factual findings supported by the evidence and cogent reasons do not warrant interference on appeal when no sufficient basis for disturbing them is shown.
material_facts: Both the trial court and the High Court found that the parties had executed the agreement for sale.
The findings were supported by the agreement and testimony from witnesses who attested it.
The High Court observed that the seller did not claim, when notified of the demand to complete the sale, that the agreement was sham or nominal; it considered the later claim an afterthought.
The Supreme Court found no case had been made out to interfere with the concurrent findings.
issues.conclusion: The concurrent findings of the lower courts were not disturbed.
issues.legal_principle: The court declined to interfere with concurrent factual findings that were supported by the evidence and cogent reasons. It cited no separate provision or precedent for this point.

rule.if: supreme_court_appeal and concurrent_fact_findings and findings_supported_by_evidence and no_contemporaneous_sham_claim

predicates.supreme_court_appeal: A party appealed to the Supreme Court against decisions of the lower courts.
predicates.concurrent_fact_findings: The trial court and the appellate court reached the same factual finding.
predicates.findings_supported_by_evidence: The shared finding was supported by documentary evidence and witness testimony.
predicates.no_contemporaneous_sham_claim: The party later alleging that the agreement was sham or nominal did not raise that claim when the other party demanded completion.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges concurrent factual findings supported by evidence, and the challenger did not contemporaneously claim the agreement was sham, the findings are not disturbed.
